phrases.english_concept: the dominant messaging platform a Taiwanese user pastes styled text into
phrases.usage_guidance: Include LINE in every zh-tw 'works on these platforms' list, alongside Instagram, Threads, Discord and 遊戲ID. Already live and correct on zh-tw/ (20 occurrences; 微信/WeChat zero). Note LINE display names and status messages are a genuine styled-text surface, not just a paste destination.
phrases.good_example: IG 簡介、LINE 暱稱、Discord 顯示名稱都可以直接貼上。
phrases.avoid_when: Never list 微信/WeChat, QQ or 微博 in TW platform lists. Do not assume LINE transfers to other locales — it is dominant in TW/JP/TH, not in MY (WhatsApp) or ID (WhatsApp).

phrases.english_concept: mojibake / garbled text — the word players use when a pasted symbol fails to render correctly on someone else's device
phrases.usage_guidance: The exact word Taiwanese players reach for when a decorative Unicode character fails cross-device. Verbatim, independently found twice on Bahamut: '進遊戲會變亂碼 很醜' (turns to mojibake in-game, ugly) and '別人手機顯示不出來...也是亂碼' (if others' phones don't show it, it's just mojibake to them). A strong candidate for FAQ framing: 'why did my name turn into 亂碼' / 'will this show as 亂碼 on other people's phones'.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as a positive/marketing term — it is exclusively a failure description.

phrases.english_concept: clan/team name — a decorable naming surface distinct from a personal nickname or a formal guild
phrases.usage_guidance: Bahamut thread '想創戰隊特殊名子' (wanting a decorated clan name) is a distinct naming job from 暱稱 (personal nickname, ZHTW-017) and 公會 (formal MMO guild, ZHTW-040) — worth a mention as a use case on a game-name generator page rather than assuming 暱稱 coverage already speaks to it.

phrases.english_concept: the Chinese ideographic comma (、) — real, sizable Semrush-confirmed volume with a weak dominant incumbent
phrases.content_surface: a hybrid page: usage rules + per-IME typing instructions + copy-paste widget
phrases.usage_guidance: Semrush db=tw (2026-08-11): 40,500/mo, KD 28. tw.piliapp.com/symbol/punctuation/ (the market's dominant incumbent) does not list 、 at all and only ranks position 9 for this term as a result -- confirmed by direct fetch, not inferred. Live-SERP verification (2026-08-11) found DUAL intent: bare/usage-rule queries are dominated by unbeatable institutional authorities (zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw, Taiwan's MOE punctuation handbook, dictionary sites); 'how do I type it' queries surface a beatable hybrid-format blog (vocus.cc) that leads with typing instructions then covers usage rules. A Bahamut thread confirms real gamer intent too: a Identity V (第五人格) board thread titled '【問題】名字怎麼打頓號' asks specifically how to type it into a game name. A prior PTT forum pass (2026-08-10) independently found 、 used AS DECORATION (not real punctuation) in some game IDs, quote: '那個不是標點符號 比較像卍或是乂的用法'.
phrases.good_example: A page that leads with 'how do I type 、 on [Windows/Mac/phone/game]' before covering correct usage -- matches what's actually winning organic real estate (vocus.cc), not a bare copy-paste tile page (which is what lost to Wikipedia/MOE on the pure-usage angle).
phrases.avoid_when: Do not build a page claiming to out-rank Wikipedia/MOE on 'correct usage' authority -- that angle is not winnable. The realistic wedge is the typing-instruction + copy-paste angle specifically.

phrases.usage_guidance: TW uses 愛心符號 (love-heart) rather than 心形符號 (heart-shaped) — 18,100/mo, the largest single keyword in the TW cut, already owned by zh-tw/library/aixin-fuhao.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid 心形 in TW-targeted copy; it reads as the geometric shape, not the affectionate glyph.
